title: Realm 1: The Spark of the Web
description: Master console output, variables with let and const, and template strings.

lessons.title: 1. Hello, JavaScript!
lessons.concept:
### Welcome to JavaScript! ⚡
JavaScript is the programming language that powers every interactive website on the planet.

In JavaScript, we use **`console.log()`** to print messages to the console.

```javascript
console.log("Hello, Web Hero!");
```

Unlike Python, JavaScript uses parentheses `()` and usually ends lines with a semicolon `;`.
lessons.task: Write a `console.log()` command that prints: `Welcome to JavaScript Hero!` exactly as shown.
lessons.starterCode:
// Write your code below and click Run Spell:
console.log("Hello, World!");
hints: Change 'Hello, World!' to 'Welcome to JavaScript Hero!'

lessons.title: 2. Variables: let vs const
lessons.task: Declare a variable `let heroName = "Volt";` and a variable `let power = 900;`. Print both using `console.log()`.

lessons.title: 3. Template Literals (`${}`)
lessons.task:
Given `const hero = "Sparky";` and `const gems = 15;`,
Use backticks to print: `Sparky collected 15 gems!`.

lessons.title: 4. Decision Making (if / else & ===)
lessons.task: Check if `let mana = 50;` is greater than or equal to 30. If so, print `Spell ready!`. Otherwise print `Need mana.`.
hints: Print 'Spell ready!' inside the if block.
Print 'Need mana.' inside the else block.

lessons.title: 5. Arrays & Push / Pop
lessons.concept:
### JavaScript Arrays `[]`
An array is a list of items:

```javascript
const inventory = ["Sword", "Shield"];
inventory.push("Magic Wand"); // Adds to end
console.log(inventory[0]); // 'Sword'
console.log(inventory.length); // 3
```
lessons.task: Start with `const team = ["Pikachu", "Charmander"];`. Use `team.push("Squirtle");` to add Squirtle, then print `team.length`.
lessons.starterCode:
const team = ["Pikachu", "Charmander"];

// Push Squirtle and print length:

lessons.title: 6. Arrow Functions
lessons.concept:
### Modern Arrow Functions `=>`
Arrow functions are clean and concise ways to write functions:

```javascript
const double = (n) => n * 2;
console.log(double(5)); // 10
```
lessons.task: Create an arrow function named `add` that takes `(a, b)` and returns `a + b`. Call `add(10, 20)` and print the result.
lessons.solution:
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(10, 20));

title: Module 2: Data Types & Type Coercion
description: Primitive types, typeof, truthy/falsy, == vs ===, explicit conversions

lessons.title: 7. Primitive Types
lessons.concept:
### Types of Toys
JavaScript has different types of values. Just like toy cars are different from stuffed animals, strings (words) are different from numbers.

Use `typeof` to find out what type a value is!
lessons.task: Use `typeof` inside `console.log()` to check the type of `"Hero"`.

lessons.title: 8. Truthy & Falsy
lessons.concept:
### Truthy & Falsy
Some values act like 'false' even if they aren't the word false. `0`, `""`, and `null` are falsy. Almost everything else is truthy!
lessons.task: Write an if statement checking `0`. If truthy print `Yes`, else print `No`.

lessons.title: 9. == vs ===
lessons.concept:
### Strict Equality
`==` compares values loosely (`"5" == 5` is true), but `===` compares strictly (types must match too!). Always use `===`!

lessons.title: 10. Explicit Conversions
lessons.concept:
### Changing Types
You can force a string into a number using `Number("5")` or a number into a string using `String(5)`.
lessons.task: Convert `"10"` to a number and print its typeof.

lessons.title: 11. Arithmetic Operators
lessons.concept:
### Math Time
Use `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, and `%` (remainder) to do math.
lessons.task: Print the remainder of 10 divided by 3.

lessons.title: 12. Logical Operators
lessons.concept:
### AND & OR
`&&` means AND (both must be true). `||` means OR (one must be true). `!` means NOT.

lessons.title: 13. Ternary Operator
lessons.concept:
### Ternary Shortcut
A shorter `if/else`: `condition ? trueValue : falseValue`.
lessons.task: Use ternary to print `Win` if `score > 50`, else `Lose`. Score is 60.

title: Module 4: Loops & Iteration
description: for, while, do...while, for...of, for...in, break/continue

lessons.title: 14. The For Loop
lessons.concept:
### Doing Things Repeatedly
A `for` loop has a start, an end condition, and a step. `for(let i = 0; i < 3; i++)` runs 3 times.
lessons.task: Write a `for` loop that prints numbers 1 to 3.

lessons.title: 15. The While Loop
lessons.concept:
### While True
A `while` loop runs as long as a condition is true.
lessons.task: Create `let count = 3` and use a while loop to print and decrease it until it hits 0.

lessons.title: 16. For...of Loop
lessons.concept:
### Loop through Arrays
`for(let item of array)` goes through every item in a list without needing a counter.
lessons.task: Loop through `['A', 'B']` and print each item.
lessons.solution: const letters = ['A', 'B']; for(let l of letters) { console.log(l); }

lessons.title: 17. Break & Continue
lessons.concept:
### Stop and Skip
`break` stops a loop entirely. `continue` skips the rest of the current turn and moves to the next.
lessons.task: Loop from 1 to 3. If i is 2, use `continue`. Print the rest.
lessons.solution: for(let i=1; i<=3; i++) { if(i === 2) continue; console.log(i); }

title: Module 5: Functions Deep Dive
description: Declaration vs expression vs arrow, default/rest params, callbacks, IIFE

lessons.title: 18. Function Expressions
lessons.concept:
### Functions as Values
You can save a function inside a variable! `const bark = function() { }`
lessons.task: Create a function expression `sayHi` that prints `Hi`. Call it.

lessons.title: 19. Default Parameters
lessons.concept:
### Backups
You can give a parameter a default value if none is passed in.
lessons.task: Create `function greet(name = "Guest")` that prints the name. Call `greet()` with nothing.

lessons.title: 20. Rest Parameters
lessons.concept:
### Gathering Arguments
`...args` collects all extra arguments into an array.
lessons.task: Create `function show(...items)` and print `items.length`. Call it with `1, 2, 3`.

lessons.title: 21. Callbacks
lessons.concept:
### Passing Functions
A callback is a function you pass to another function to be run later.
lessons.task: Create `runCallback(cb)` that calls `cb()`. Pass a function that prints `Done`.

title: Module 6: Objects & JSON
description: Object literals, dot/bracket notation, Object.keys/values/entries, JSON.stringify/parse

lessons.title: 22. Object Literals
lessons.concept:
### Data Containers
Objects hold data using keys and values. `const car = { color: 'red' }`.
lessons.task: Create an object `player` with `name: 'Hero'` and `score: 100`. Print `player.name`.

lessons.title: 23. Bracket Notation
lessons.concept:
### Dynamic Keys
You can access object properties using brackets `[]` instead of a dot. Useful when keys have spaces!

lessons.title: 24. Object Methods
lessons.concept:
### Getting Keys
`Object.keys(obj)` returns an array of all the keys in an object.
lessons.task: Print the keys of `{ a: 1, b: 2 }` using `Object.keys()`.

lessons.title: 25. JSON
lessons.concept:
### Stringifying
JSON is a text format for objects. `JSON.stringify(obj)` turns an object into a JSON string.
lessons.task: Convert `{ name: 'Bot' }` to a string and print it.

title: Module 7: Destructuring & Spread
description: Array destructuring, object destructuring, spread operator

lessons.title: 26. Array Destructuring
lessons.concept:
### Unpacking Arrays
Extract values easily: `const [a, b] = [1, 2]` assigns 1 to a and 2 to b.

lessons.title: 27. Object Destructuring
lessons.concept:
### Unpacking Objects
Extract properties: `const { name } = { name: 'Hero' }` assigns 'Hero' to name.
lessons.task: Extract `age` from `{ age: 12, name: 'Alex' }` and print it.

lessons.title: 28. Spread Operator
lessons.concept:
### Spreading Values
The spread operator `...` unpacks elements. `[...arr1, ...arr2]` combines arrays.
lessons.task: Combine `[1, 2]` and `[3, 4]` using spread and print the new array's length.
lessons.solution: const arr1 = [1, 2]; const arr2 = [3, 4]; const combined = [...arr1, ...arr2]; console.log(combined.length);

lessons.title: 29. Array Map
lessons.concept:
### Transforming Arrays
`map` runs a function on every item and returns a new array with the results.
lessons.task: Use `.map()` on `[1, 2, 3]` to double each number. Print the new array.
lessons.solution: const nums = [1, 2, 3]; const doubled = nums.map(n => n * 2); console.log(doubled);

lessons.title: 30. Array Filter
lessons.concept:
### Filtering Arrays
`filter` keeps only the items that pass a test.
lessons.task: Filter `[1, 2, 3, 4]` to keep numbers greater than 2.
lessons.solution: const nums = [1, 2, 3, 4]; const big = nums.filter(n => n > 2); console.log(big);

lessons.title: 31. Array Reduce
lessons.concept:
### Reducing Arrays
`reduce` combines all items into a single value, like a sum.
lessons.starterCode:
const sum = [1, 2, 3].reduce((acc, n) => acc + n, 0);
console.log(sum);
lessons.solution: const sum = [1, 2, 3].reduce((acc, n) => acc + n, 0); console.log(sum);

lessons.title: 32. Find & Some
lessons.concept:
### Searching
`find` gets the first match. `some` checks if *any* match exists.
lessons.task: Use `.find()` on `[10, 20, 30]` to get the number equal to 20.

lessons.title: 33. Chaining Methods
lessons.concept:
### Combo Moves
You can string methods together! `.filter().map()`
lessons.task: Filter `[1, 2, 3]` for > 1, then map to multiply by 10. Print result.

title: Module 9: Scope, Hoisting & Closures
description: Block vs function scope, hoisting, closures, practical closures

lessons.title: 34. Block Scope
lessons.concept:
### Variable Visibility
Variables made with `let` inside `{ }` are locked in there!
lessons.task: Create a block with `{ let x = 5; }`. Try to log `typeof x` outside.

lessons.title: 35. Closures
lessons.concept:
### Backpacks
A closure is a function that remembers its outer variables even after it is returned.
lessons.task: Create a function returning `() => 'Hello'`. Call it.

lessons.title: 36. Practical Closures
lessons.concept:
### Using Closures
You can make private counters using closures.
lessons.task: Write a counter function that increments and returns a variable.
lessons.solution: function counter() { let c = 0; return () => ++c; } const next = counter(); console.log(next());

lessons.title: 37. Hoisting
lessons.concept:
### Floating Up
Function declarations are 'hoisted' (moved) to the top of the file, so you can call them before you define them.

lessons.title: 38. Try/Catch
lessons.concept:
### Safety Nets
Use `try` to run code that might fail, and `catch` to handle errors without crashing.
lessons.task: Wrap `unknownFunction()` in a try/catch and log `"Caught it!"` in the catch.

lessons.title: 39. Throwing Errors
lessons.concept:
### Raising Flags
Use `throw new Error('msg')` to create your own errors.
lessons.task: Throw an Error, catch it, and print its `.message`.
lessons.solution: try { throw new Error("Bad"); } catch (e) { console.log(e.message); }

lessons.title: 40. Finally
lessons.concept:
### Always Runs
`finally` block runs whether there was an error or not.
lessons.task: Add a finally block to print `"Done"`.

lessons.title: 41. Classes & Constructors
lessons.concept:
### Factories
A class is a blueprint. The `constructor` runs when you create a new instance using `new`.
lessons.task: Create a `class Hero` with a `constructor(name)` that sets `this.name`. Print `new Hero('Batman').name`.
lessons.solution: class Hero { constructor(name) { this.name = name; } } console.log(new Hero('Batman').name);

lessons.title: 42. Methods
lessons.concept:
### Actions
Methods are functions inside a class.
lessons.task: Add a `speak()` method to `Hero` that returns `"I am Hero"`.
lessons.solution: class Hero { speak() { return "I am Hero"; } } console.log(new Hero().speak());

lessons.title: 43. Extends & Super
lessons.concept:
### Inheritance
Use `extends` to base a class on another, and `super()` to call the parent's constructor.
lessons.solution: class Hero { constructor(name) { this.name = name; } } class Mage extends Hero { constructor(name) { super(name); } } console.log(new Mage('Merlin').name);

lessons.title: 44. Static Methods
lessons.concept:
### Class-Level Methods
Static methods belong to the class itself, not the instances.
lessons.task: Add `static info()` returning `"Class"` and call it as `Hero.info()`.
lessons.solution: class Hero { static info() { return "Class"; } } console.log(Hero.info());

lessons.title: 45. querySelector
lessons.concept:
### Finding Elements
`document.querySelector()` finds an element on the webpage. (Simulated in this lesson)
lessons.task: Log `"Found element"` as if you ran querySelector.

lessons.title: 46. Modifying Content
lessons.concept:
### Changing HTML
You can change `.innerHTML` or `.textContent` of an element. (Simulated)

lessons.title: 47. Creating Elements
lessons.concept:
### New HTML
`document.createElement('div')` makes a new element! (Simulated)

lessons.title: 48. addEventListener
lessons.concept:
### Listening for Clicks
`.addEventListener('click', fn)` runs code when clicked! (Simulated)

lessons.title: 49. Event Delegation
lessons.concept:
### Smart Listening
Listen on a parent element instead of many children! (Simulated)

lessons.title: 50. localStorage
lessons.concept:
### Saving Data
`localStorage.setItem('key', 'value')` saves data permanently in the browser! (Simulated)

lessons.title: 51. setTimeout
lessons.concept:
### Delays
`setTimeout(fn, 1000)` waits 1 second before running code.

lessons.title: 52. Date Object
lessons.concept:
### Current Time
`new Date()` gets the current date and time.

lessons.title: 53. Navigator
lessons.concept:
### Browser Info
`navigator.userAgent` tells you about the browser. (Simulated)

title: Module 14: Async & Promises
description: Event loop, callback hell, Promise .then/.catch, creating Promises

lessons.title: 54. Event Loop
lessons.concept:
### Non-Blocking
JS handles heavy tasks in the background and continues running the rest of the code.

lessons.title: 55. Creating Promises
lessons.concept:
### I Promise
A Promise represents a future value. `new Promise((resolve, reject) => ...)`.
lessons.task: Create a Promise that resolves with `"Done"`. Call `.then(console.log)` on it.

lessons.title: 56. Promise Chaining
lessons.concept:
### Step by Step
You can return a value in a `.then()` and catch it in the next `.then()`.
lessons.task: Resolve `1`, then return `val + 1`, then print it.

lessons.title: 57. Catching Errors
lessons.concept:
### Oops
Use `.catch()` to handle Promise rejections.
lessons.task: Reject a Promise with `"Error"` and catch it, printing the message.

title: Module 15: Async/Await & Fetch
description: async/await, try/catch with await, fetch API, Promise.all/race

lessons.title: 58. Async / Await
lessons.concept:
### Pausing Code
`await` pauses a function until a Promise finishes! Must be inside an `async` function.
lessons.task: Create an async function that awaits `Promise.resolve('Awaited')` and logs it.

lessons.title: 59. Fetch API
lessons.concept:
### Getting Data
`fetch()` grabs data from the internet. (Simulated)

lessons.title: 60. Promise.all
lessons.concept:
### Doing it all at once
`Promise.all([p1, p2])` waits for all promises to finish.
lessons.solution: (async () => { const res = await Promise.all([Promise.resolve(1), Promise.resolve(2)]); console.log(res.length); })();

lessons.title: 61. Promise.race
lessons.concept:
### The Winner
`Promise.race()` takes an array of promises and resolves with the first one to finish.

title: Module 16: Modules & Tooling
description: ES Modules import/export, CommonJS require, dynamic import()

lessons.title: 62. ES Modules Export
lessons.concept:
### Sharing Code
`export const x = 5;` lets other files use your variable. (Simulated)

lessons.title: 63. ES Modules Import
lessons.concept:
### Using Code
`import { x } from './file.js';` gets code from another file. (Simulated)

lessons.title: 64. CommonJS
lessons.concept:
### Older Modules
Node.js uses `require('module')`. (Simulated)

lessons.title: 65. RegExp test
lessons.concept:
### Pattern Matching
`/hello/.test('hello world')` checks if 'hello' is in the string.
lessons.task: Test if `/abc/` is in `"xabcy"` and print the boolean result.

lessons.title: 66. String match
lessons.concept:
### Finding Matches
`'hello'.match(/e/)` returns info about where the match happened.
lessons.task: Match `"123"` for digits using `/[0-9]+/` and log the first result `res[0]`.

lessons.title: 67. String replace
lessons.concept:
### Replacing
`'cat'.replace(/a/, 'o')` returns 'cot'.
lessons.task: Replace 'bad' with 'good' in 'bad dog' and print.

lessons.title: 68. Maps
lessons.concept:
### Super Objects
A `Map` is like an object but keys can be *anything*, even other objects!
lessons.solution: const m = new Map(); m.set('a', 1); console.log(m.get('a'));

lessons.title: 69. Sets
lessons.concept:
### Unique Arrays
A `Set` is a collection of unique values. Duplicates disappear automatically!
lessons.task: Create a `new Set([1, 1, 2])` and print its `.size`.

lessons.title: 70. Symbols
lessons.concept:
### Hidden Keys
`Symbol('desc')` creates a unique identifier, often used as hidden keys in objects.

lessons.title: 71. Iterators
lessons.concept:
### Stepping Through
An iterator allows you to step through data using `.next()`.

lessons.title: 72. Generators
lessons.concept:
### Pause and Play
A generator function `function*` can pause execution with `yield` and resume later.
lessons.task: Create a generator `function* gen() { yield 1; }` and print `gen().next().value`.

lessons.title: 73. Proxies
lessons.concept:
### Traps
A `Proxy` lets you intercept and change how objects behave.

lessons.title: 74. Reflect
lessons.concept:
### Mirrors
`Reflect` provides methods to intercept JavaScript operations.

lessons.title: 75. Pure Functions
lessons.concept:
### No Side Effects
Pure functions always return the same result for the same input and don't change outside variables.
lessons.task: Write `const add = (a, b) => a + b;` and print `add(2, 2)`.
lessons.starterCode:
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(2, 2));
lessons.solution: const add = (a, b) => a + b; console.log(add(2, 2));

lessons.title: 76. Currying
lessons.concept:
### Russian Dolls
Currying turns `f(a, b)` into `f(a)(b)`. `const add = a => b => a + b;`
lessons.starterCode:
const add = a => b => a + b;
console.log(add(2)(3));
lessons.solution: const add = a => b => a + b; console.log(add(2)(3));

lessons.title: 77. Composition
lessons.concept:
### Piping
Composition is combining multiple functions to create a new one.

### Types (Simulated)
